resources.string: Learn Goals
Learn Goals in a few steps
Try a short guide with sample goals. Your real goals stay unchanged.
Practice mode · Sample goals
Close the current goal form or action and wait for saving to finish before starting practice.
Revise one chapter
Read the notes and review the examples.
Revise two sections
What would you like to learn?
How to create and finish a goal
Plan or repeat a goal
Repeat a routine
Edit or recover a goal
Handle missed goals
Review your progress
Add a goal
Choose Add goal.
Start with one clear study task. Next opens a sample form; no real goal is created.
Name and create your goal
Name your task, then choose Create Goal.
Write one clear task. Details, a future date, and daily repeat are optional. Next shows the sample goal in Today.
Create the goal
Use Create goal when ready.
A new goal belongs to Today unless you schedule a future date. Next shows the sample goal in Today.
Work on today’s goal
Find your task in Today.
Today shows goals available to work on now. Read the title and any details before starting your study work.
Mark your goal done
Find it in Today and tap its checkbox.
Use the checkbox when the task is finished. It opens the study-time and completion choices.
Record study time
Enter time, or use quick-add chips.
Hours and minutes record manual study time. You can also complete without adding time. Avoid entering the same time again if Ekagra already recorded it.
Add time and finish
Add time if needed, then tap Done.
Use hours, minutes, or quick-add chips. Done saves the time and finishes the goal. Complete without study time adds no minutes. Do not add time that Ekagra already recorded.
Review completed goals
Open History to review your work.
History groups completed goals by their assigned day. Choose a date to review that day. The sample entry disappears when practice closes.
Plan ahead
Enable Schedule for a future day.
Goals default to Today. Choose the future-day option when the work belongs to a later date.
Choose a future day
Turn on Schedule and pick a date.
Choose Schedule for a future date, then pick the day. Create the goal when ready. This sample uses tomorrow.
Find scheduled work
Review future goals in Upcoming.
A scheduled goal appears in Upcoming before its assigned day. It becomes available in Today when that day arrives.
Build a daily routine
Enable Repeat every day if needed.
Use daily repeat for recurring work. Completing one day’s goal does not mean all future days are complete.
Reuse your tasks
Use Repeat Goals to copy selected tasks.
Open Repeat Goals from the action row. Choose today’s tasks for tomorrow, or yesterday’s tasks for today. Automatic repeat makes a daily routine.
Repeat selected work daily
Use automatic repeat for a routine.
When repeating today’s goals for tomorrow, the automatic-repeat option turns the selected tasks into a daily routine.
Bring yesterday’s work forward
Choose Yesterday in Repeat Goals.
Yesterday lets you select tasks to bring into today. Next changes only the sample view; it never duplicates real goals.
Manage a goal
Open the goal’s three-dot menu.
An open goal offers editing, completion, and deletion actions. Completed goals can be reopened when the action is available.
Adjust your plan
Edit the title or details, then save.
Use Edit on an open goal to update its task, schedule, or daily-repeat choice. Practice uses the same form with a sample title.
Recover a deleted goal
Open Recently deleted and choose Restore.
Deletion has a confirmation and recovery is available for 30 days. Restore returns the goal to its appropriate date; an old goal may still be missed.
Handle missed work
Open Missed to finish or reschedule old tasks.
Missed holds unfinished goals from earlier days. Complete one or edit its date. When completing, you can keep its original day or move it to today.
Choose the completion date
Keep the original date, or move to today.
After entering study time for an older goal, choose whether to complete it for its original day or move it to today and complete it. Cancel keeps it open.
Check your progress
Open Status for a quick overview.
Status summarizes open, missed, scheduled, and completed goals. These numbers are sample data in practice.
Explore your trends
Use Insights for goal analytics.
Insights opens the Goals analytics screen in normal use. The tutorial highlights the entry without navigating or loading account data.
Connect focus and goals
Link a goal when saving an Ekagra session.
In Ekagra’s save flow, select a goal and choose whether to keep it open or mark it done. Goals History shows linked focus contributions after completion. Do not log the same minutes again manually.
